mazos.descripcion: Verbos modales (can, could, may, might, must, have to, should, would…): significado, completar, elegir, traducir, reescribir y errores típicos.

campos: I advise you to leave now, or you'll miss the bus.
You'd better leave now, or you'll miss the bus.
You ___ pay to enter the museum. It's free!
You don't have to pay to enter the museum. It's free!
You ___ have seen John yesterday. He's in Japan.
You can't have seen John yesterday. He's in Japan.
It was a mistake not to study.
He {{c1::must}} be really rich. Look at his car!
Debe de ser muy rico. ¡Mira su coche!
You ___ see a dentist about that tooth.
You should see a dentist about that tooth.
{{c1::Can}} you help me with my homework?
You {{c1::shouldn't}} go to bed so late.
Tienes que llevar puesto el cinturón.
Se dice wear o put on a seatbelt.
I will can help you next week.
I will be able to help you next week.
No se ponen dos modales juntos.
Más vale que no llegues tarde.
no tener que / no hace falta
You don't have to come if you don't want to.
No tienes que venir si no quieres.
No es prohibición: puedes hacerlo si quieres.
Tengo que llamar a mi madre esta noche.
Para reglas externas (leyes, trabajo) se prefiere have to.
You {{c1::mustn't}} touch that cable. It's dangerous!
He can to play the piano.
I would travel more if I had more money.
Viajaría más si tuviera más dinero.
I'm sure she isn't the teacher.
You ___ wear a tie. It's a casual party.
You don't have to wear a tie. It's a casual party.
You {{c1::needn't}} bring anything. We have plenty of food.
No hace falta que traigas nada. Tenemos comida de sobra.
= You don't have to bring anything.
I'll be able to help you tomorrow.
can no tiene futuro ni infinitivo: will can → will be able to.
I had to wait for two hours.
When I was young, I ___ run ten kilometres without stopping.
When I was young, I could run ten kilometres without stopping.
I might go to the party, but I don't know yet.
A lo mejor voy a la fiesta, pero aún no lo sé.
Suele indicar algo menos de certeza que may.
Es incontable: an advice advices → a piece of advice. El verbo es advise.
I'll be able to see you on Monday.
We {{c1::don't have to}} wear a suit to the office.
No tenemos que llevar traje a la oficina.
You're not allowed to use your phone here.
Don't worry, we have plenty of time.
Mi hermano sabe cocinar muy bien.
You'd better hurry, or you'll miss the train.
Más vale que te des prisa o perderás el tren.
Hurry up! = ¡Date prisa! · in a hurry = con prisa.
We ___ go to the cinema tonight. What do you think?
We could go to the cinema tonight. What do you think?
He must have forget his keys.
I hope I'll ___ come to your wedding.
I hope I'll be able to come to your wedding.
Después de will no puede ir can.
Los modales no usan do en preguntas: se invierte el orden.
I'm sure they forgot about the meeting.
They must have forgotten about the meeting.
Deducción sobre el pasado: must have + participio.
Students {{c1::mustn't}} use their phones during the exam.
Los estudiantes no pueden usar el móvil durante el examen.
It can get very cold here in winter.
Aquí puede hacer mucho frío en invierno.
Habla de lo que es posible en general, no de una predicción concreta.
You look pale. You {{c1::should}} go home and rest.
Tienes mala cara. Deberías irte a casa a descansar.
You ___ have told me! I would have helped you.
You should have told me! I would have helped you.
Reproche: «deberías habérmelo dicho». must have sería una deducción.
We ___ wear a uniform at my school. It's the rule.
We have to wear a uniform at my school. It's the rule.
Es una norma (obligación), no un consejo.
Se le debe de haber olvidado.
No tienes que venir si no quieres.
You don't have to come if you don't want to.
Va al final de la frase.
Decisión tomada en el momento de hablar.
That {{c1::can't}} be Tom. He's in London this week.
Ese no puede ser Tom. Está en Londres esta semana.
No debes fumar en el hospital.
Can you remind me to call Ana?
remember = acordarte tú. remind = hacer que otro se acuerde.
Do you know how to drive?
Te avisé del tiempo que iba a hacer.
Con will va entre will y el verbo.
Arrepentimiento o crítica sobre el pasado
Algo que no hiciste (y estuvo mal no hacerlo).
I'm sure he didn't take it.
Deducción negativa sobre el pasado: can't have + participio.
I {{c1::would}} buy a house if I had enough money.
Me compraría una casa si tuviera suficiente dinero.
Her eyes are red. She {{c1::must have}} been crying.
Tiene los ojos rojos. Debe de haber estado llorando.
I {{c1::can}} play the guitar, but not very well.
Sé tocar la guitarra, pero no muy bien.
Deducción negativa (estoy seguro de que NO)
Es lo contrario de must (deducción). Para esto NO se usa mustn't.
I'm exhausted. I {{c1::should have}} gone to bed earlier.
Estoy agotado. Debería haberme acostado antes.
Deducción sobre el pasado (seguro que SÍ)
Se le debe de haber olvidado.
You ___ park here. It's a fire exit.
You mustn't park here. It's a fire exit.
Would you like me to open the window?
The lights are on. They {{c1::must}} be at home.
Las luces están encendidas. Deben de estar en casa.
Casi solo en preguntas con I o we: Shall I help you?
I could swim when I was five.
Sabía nadar cuando tenía cinco años.
Habilidad general en el pasado. Para un logro concreto se usa was able to: I was able to fix it.
They {{c1::must have}} gone out. The lights are off.
Deben de haber salido. Las luces están apagadas.
It's polite to say please and thank you.
Es de buena educación decir por favor y gracias.
I don't have to get up early tomorrow.
wake up = despertarse. get up = levantarse de la cama.
No hace falta que traigas nada.
También: She / I might not come.
No seas maleducado con tu hermana.
I'm sure he is at home.
Is it OK if I sit here? (formal)
When I was a child, I {{c1::could}} climb trees easily.
Cuando era niño, podía trepar a los árboles fácilmente.
Me gustaría un vaso de agua.
I'd like a glass of water.
You should see a dentist about that tooth.
Deberías ir al dentista por esa muela.
It's a secret. You ___ tell anyone.
It's a secret. You mustn't tell anyone.
Tomorrow is Sunday, so I {{c1::don't have to}} get up early.
Mañana es domingo, así que no tengo que madrugar.
We missed the bus by two minutes.
Perdimos el autobús por dos minutos.
También: I miss you = te echo de menos. Perder un objeto = lose.
No hace falta que me esperes.
You don't have to wait for me.
Irregular: steal – stole – stolen. Robar a una persona o un banco = rob.
It wasn't necessary for us to wait.
He's only six, so he {{c1::can't}} drive.
Solo tiene seis años, así que no puede conducir.
His car is still here. He ___ have taken the bus.
His car is still here. He must have taken the bus.
Deducción sobre el pasado: seguro que sí.
Puede que hayan perdido el autobús.
Más vale que te des prisa.
«Saber + infinitivo» (sé nadar, sé conducir) se dice con can: I can swim.
Dogs are not allowed in the shop.
No se permiten perros en la tienda.
be allowed to + verbo: Am I allowed to park here?
Después del modal, verbo en infinitivo (sin -s).
Consejo (igual que should, algo más formal)
I was able to run fast when I was young.
I could run fast when I was young.
I ___ go out tonight, but I'm not sure yet.
I might go out tonight, but I'm not sure yet.
I'm sorry, I won't {{c1::be able to}} come to your party.
Lo siento, no podré ir a tu fiesta.
ablehelpI'llyoubetotomorrow
I'll be able to help you tomorrow.
Posibilidad en el pasado: might have + participio.
Take an umbrella. It {{c1::might}} rain later.
Llévate un paraguas. Puede que llueva luego.
Estaba escondido detrás de la puerta.
You must to wear a helmet.
I {{c1::could have}} passed the exam if I had studied.
Podría haber aprobado el examen si hubiera estudiado.
I ___ swim when I was three.
I couldn't swim when I was three.
mindtheyouclosingwoulddoor
I'm not sure, but she {{c1::might}} be at the library.
No estoy seguro, pero puede que esté en la biblioteca.
We could go to the beach tomorrow.
Podríamos ir a la playa mañana.
My parents don't allow me to go out at night.
Mis padres no me dejan salir por la noche.
Podía trepar a los árboles fácilmente.
{{c1::Could}} you pass me the salt, please?
Can también vale, pero could es más cortés.
We could go to the cinema.
She {{c1::has to}} work on Saturdays. Her boss says so.
Tiene que trabajar los sábados. Lo dice su jefe.
have to sí se conjuga: she has to.
follow / break the rules = cumplir / saltarse las normas.
We'd {{c1::better}} not be late for the interview.
Más vale que no lleguemos tarde a la entrevista.
It isn't possible that she is 40.
You ___ use a pen. A pencil is fine too.
You don't have to use a pen. A pencil is fine too.
My advice is to take a break.
It's possible that he is ill.
When she was young, she {{c1::couldn't}} swim.
Perhaps they didn't get the message.
They might not have got the message.
Se le debe de haber olvidado.
También: He / They must have forgotten.
En preguntas, el modal va delante del sujeto.
You'd better hurry, or you'll miss the train.
Más vale que te des prisa o perderás el tren.
'd better + verbo sin to. Implica una consecuencia negativa. Negativa: had better not.
She don't have to work today.
have to se conjuga con does / doesn't.
I have to wear a uniform at work.
Tengo que llevar uniforme en el trabajo.
Se conjuga: has to, had to, will have to. El pasado de must es had to.
I hope I'll be able to come to your wedding.
Espero poder ir a tu boda.
___ I help you with your bags?
Shall I help you with your bags?
You {{c1::mustn't}} tell anyone. It's a secret.
No se lo debes contar a nadie. Es un secreto.
I have to wear a uniform at work.
Tengo que llevar uniforme en el trabajo.
She ___ be at work. I've just seen her at the gym.
She can't be at work. I've just seen her at the gym.
I can't find my keys. I ___ have left them at the office.
I can't find my keys. I must have left them at the office.
After three hours, I finally ___ fix my bike.
After three hours, I finally was able to fix my bike.
Para un logro concreto en el pasado se usa was able to (o managed to), no could.
You'd {{c1::better}} leave now, or you'll be late.
Más vale que te vayas ya o llegarás tarde.
En negativas y preguntas se usa yet: Have you finished yet?
Los modales no llevan -s en 3ª persona.
It isn't necessary to bring food.
You {{c1::can't}} park here. It's a private garage.
No puedes aparcar aquí. Es un garaje privado.
can't también expresa prohibición (más informal que mustn't).
He's been yawning all evening. He ___ be tired.
He's been yawning all evening. He must be tired.
You ___ better study for the exam.
You had better study for the exam.
They {{c1::might have}} got lost. Let's call them.
Puede que se hayan perdido. Llamémoslos.
I ___ like a cup of tea, please.
I would like a cup of tea, please.
He {{c1::can't have}} seen me. I was hiding behind the door.
No puede haberme visto. Estaba escondido detrás de la puerta.
Ayer tuve que trabajar hasta tarde.
must no tiene pasado: se usa had to.
I {{c1::will}} call you tomorrow, I promise.
Te llamo mañana, te lo prometo.
She ___ be French. Her accent is perfect.
She must be French. Her accent is perfect.
I don't like tea. Can I have coffee instead?
No me gusta el té. ¿Puedo tomar café en su lugar?
instead of + sustantivo o -ing: instead of going out.
It's a good idea to book a table.
In my country you {{c1::have to}} be 18 to vote.
En mi país hay que tener 18 años para votar.
It was necessary for me to work on Sunday.
apologize for algo: He apologized for being late.
Can I go to the bathroom?
Más formal: May I go to the bathroom?
You didn't have to do that.
Hay que tener 18 años para votar.
No hace falta que te preocupes.
Deducción positiva (estoy casi seguro de que SÍ)
You've been working all day. You must be tired.
Llevas todo el día trabajando. Debes de estar cansado.
Lo contrario es can't: You can't be tired!
I couldn't swim when I was a child.
Se le debe de haber olvidado mi cumpleaños.
¿Existe una regla absoluta de que will es para futuro lejano y going to para futuro cercano?
No. Ambos pueden referirse a un futuro cercano o lejano.
La elección suele depender del contexto: decisión espontánea, plan previo, opinión o evidencia presente. El tiempo que falta no basta.
Evita elegir la estructura contando días.
an interview that lasts fifty minutes
Cuando una medida forma un adjetivo antes del sustantivo, la unidad va en singular: fifty-minute.
What does she ___ to do to pass the course?
What does she need to do to pass the course?
Need to expresa necesidad. Con does, need queda en forma base. Significa: «¿Qué necesita hacer para aprobar el curso?».
What does she need to do to pass the course?
It is unlikely to rain tomorrow.
Probablemente no lloverá → es poco probable que llueva. La negación de won't queda representada por unlikely.
«It is unlikely not to rain» invertiría el sentido.
It is unlikely to rain tomorrow.
Despite the difficulty, I managed ___ the report
Despite the difficulty, I managed to finish the report.
Manage se construye con to + verbo base. Aquí significa «lograr terminar».
Despite the difficulty, I managed to finish the report.
En «I've already chosen the experiment. I'm going to start tomorrow», ¿qué comunica going to?
Una intención decidida previamente: empezaré mañana.
Already chosen indica que la decisión es anterior al momento de hablar. Going to encaja con ese contexto.
No elijas will solo porque aparece tomorrow: ambos pueden referirse al futuro.
Tomorrow I will ___ attend the meeting
Tomorrow I will be able to attend the meeting.
Para capacidad futura: will + be able to + verbo base. Significa: «Mañana podré asistir a la reunión».
No omitas be ni combines «will can».
Tomorrow I will be able to attend the meeting.
He won't come tomorrow. / He will not come tomorrow.
Won't es la contracción de will not. Significa: «Él no vendrá mañana».
He won't come tomorrow. / He will not come tomorrow.
Under pressure significa bajo presión. Es una combinación habitual al hablar de habilidades laborales.
Forma el adjetivo con English + speak
English-speaking significa que habla inglés. Speaking describe lo que hace el guía.
They managed to find a solution
They succeeded in finding a solution.
El significado básico se mantiene, pero cambia el patrón: managed to find → succeeded in finding.
No conserves el infinitivo después de in.
They succeeded in finding a solution.
Scenery significa el paisaje o las vistas de una zona y normalmente es incontable. Por eso usamos scenery + is.
Evita sceneries en este uso general.
La combinación habitual es make an effort: hacer un esfuerzo.
No traduzcas automáticamente hacer como do: «do an effort» es incorrecto.
Completa con couldn't para una prohibición habitual
At my old job, we ___ check personal emails during work
At my old job, we couldn't check personal emails during work.
En un contexto de reglas pasadas, couldn't expresa falta de permiso. Significa: «No podíamos revisar correos personales durante el trabajo».
No uses mustn't para marcar el pasado de esa regla.
At my old job, we couldn't check personal emails during work.
Outdoor activities, for ___ hiking, can help you relax
Outdoor activities, for example hiking, can help you relax.
For example introduce un caso que ilustra una idea general. Hiking es un ejemplo de actividad al aire libre. También: «Outdoor activities, such as hiking, …».
For example no introduce por sí mismo una consecuencia como therefore.
Outdoor activities, for example hiking, can help you relax.
My room is full. I've run out ___ space
My room is full. I've run out of space.
Run out of + sustantivo significa quedarse sin algo. Aquí: «Me he quedado sin espacio».
My room is full. I've run out of space.
Look at those dark clouds! It ___ rain
Look at those dark clouds! It is going to rain.
La predicción se apoya en evidencia presente: las nubes oscuras. Significa: «Va a llover».
No confundas este uso con un plan voluntario de las nubes.
Look at those dark clouds! It is going to rain.
She can ___ people to try new ideas
She can persuade people to try new ideas.
Persuade + persona + to + verbo base: convencer a alguien de que haga algo.
No omitas to delante de try.
She can persuade people to try new ideas.
We decided yesterday. We ___ visit Cusco next month
We are going to visit Cusco next month.
Be going to expresa una intención o plan decidido antes de hablar. Con we usamos are.
We are going to visit Cusco next month.
Completa en pasado con have to. Expresa ausencia de obligación.
Last Friday, the office was closed, so we ___ go to work
Last Friday, the office was closed, so we didn't have to go to work.
Didn't have to significa «no tuvimos que»: no había obligación. La estructura por sí sola no asegura si finalmente fuimos.
No confundas didn't have to con weren't allowed to.
Last Friday, the office was closed, so we didn't have to go to work.
Do I must wear a tie?
Must forma preguntas sin do: must + sujeto + verbo base. También sería posible preguntar «Do I have to wear a tie?».
We haven't decided. We ___ take a ferry
We haven't decided. We might take a ferry.
Might + verbo base expresa posibilidad sin confirmarla: «Quizá tomemos un ferry».
We haven't decided. We might take a ferry.
Make yourself at home es una invitación a ponerse cómodo y actuar con confianza: «Siéntete como en casa».
After an hour, we ___ able to repair the bike
After an hour, we were able to repair the bike.
Con we, el pasado de be es were. Were able to sirve para un logro concreto: pudimos reparar la bicicleta.
After an hour, we were able to repair the bike.
Landscape puede ser contable: a landscape, two landscapes. Aquí es un paisaje de montaña representado en una pintura.
No supongas que landscape y scenery tienen idéntico comportamiento contable.
Después de did/didn't, el verbo vuelve a su forma base. Significa: «Ella no logró terminar».
El pasado ya está en didn't; no lo marques otra vez en managed.
Will definitely expresa una predicción presentada con mucha seguridad: «Sin duda terminaremos hoy».
La seguridad del hablante no garantiza el resultado real.
Can you ___ a team of ten people?
Can you manage a team of ten people?
Manage a team significa dirigir o gestionar un equipo. Aquí manage lleva un sustantivo como objeto.
No necesita to: no es la estructura manage to + verbo.
Can you manage a team of ten people?
Con will, la pregunta empieza por el modal: will + sujeto + verbo base. Significa: «¿Llegará antes del mediodía?».
Pide permiso de forma cortés usando could
Could I…? es una forma cortés de pedir permiso presente o futuro. Aquí could no habla del pasado.
No traduzcas automáticamente cada could como pasado.
Completa con will para ofrecer ayuda
Your bag looks heavy. I ___ carry it for you
Your bag looks heavy. I'll carry it for you.
I'll + verbo base sirve para ofrecer ayuda espontáneamente: «Yo te la llevo».
Your bag looks heavy. I'll carry it for you.
Completa usando likely. Expresa que ganar es probable.
Be likely to + verbo base significa «es probable que». Expresa probabilidad, no certeza.
Completa con can para dar permiso
You ___ use my calculator during the break
You can use my calculator during the break.
Can también expresa permiso: «Puedes usar mi calculadora». El contexto indica autorización, no habilidad matemática.
You can use my calculator during the break.
Hard-working significa trabajadora o que se esfuerza mucho. No es lo mismo que hardly working, que significa que apenas trabaja.
No cambies hard por hardly: el significado cambia mucho.
¿May y might indican porcentajes fijos de probabilidad, como 50 % y 30 %?
No. Sus interpretaciones dependen del contexto.
Ambos expresan posibilidad. Might puede sonar más tentativo en algunos contextos, pero no hay una escala numérica universal.
No memorices porcentajes inventados como reglas gramaticales.
Did you manage to solve the problem?
Pregunta en pasado: did + sujeto + manage to + verbo base. Significa: «¿Lograste resolver el problema?».
Did you manage to solve the problem?
Completa la instrucción con imperativo. Usa fold.
Para dar instrucciones usamos el verbo base sin sujeto explícito. First marca el primer paso. Significa: «Primero, dobla el papel por la mitad».
No escribas «First, to fold…» como instrucción completa.
you / are / going to / apply / for the job / ?
Are you going to apply for the job?
La pregunta invierte be y sujeto: are + you + going to + apply. Significa: «¿Vas a postular al trabajo?».
Are you going to apply for the job?
Después de can va el verbo base sin to. Significa: «Sé nadar».
No uses «to swim» después de can.
How do you deal ___ difficult problems?
How do you deal with difficult problems?
Deal with significa afrontar, manejar o tratar un problema. La preposición de esta expresión es with.
How do you deal with difficult problems?
Yesterday I ___ to show my passport
Yesterday I had to show my passport.
Para una obligación pasada usamos had to. Significa: «Ayer tuve que mostrar mi pasaporte».
No uses must como forma de pasado en este ejercicio.
Yesterday I had to show my passport.
Completa con have to en futuro
Next year we ___ renew our permits
Next year we will have to renew our permits.
Will have to expresa obligación futura. Significa: «El próximo año tendremos que renovar nuestros permisos».
Next year we will have to renew our permits.
I promise I ___ call you tonight
I promise I'll call you tonight. / I promise I will call you tonight.
Will se usa en promesas. Significa: «Prometo que te llamaré esta noche».
I promise I'll call you tonight. / I promise I will call you tonight.
Managers often have to ___ difficult decisions
Managers often have to make difficult decisions.
Make decisions significa tomar decisiones. Con difficult: tomar decisiones difíciles.
Managers often have to make difficult decisions.
Completa la pregunta con have to
En presente simple: does + sujeto + have to. Significa: «¿Ella tiene que trabajar los domingos?».
Después de does va have, no has.
We took a ferry from the island to the ___
We took a ferry from the island to the mainland.
Mainland es la masa principal de tierra frente a una isla. Se puede traducir como tierra firme o territorio continental, según el lugar.
Island designa la isla, no la masa principal de tierra.
We took a ferry from the island to the mainland.
Are you good at ___ with other people?
Are you good at working with other people?
Good at working with other people significa ser bueno trabajando con otras personas. At exige -ing si lo sigue un verbo.
Evita «good in work» para expresar esta idea.
Are you good at working with other people?
Could you tell me when does the bus leave?
Could you tell me when the bus leaves?
En una pregunta indirecta, la parte introducida por when usa orden afirmativo: sujeto + verbo. Could you tell me…? ya forma la pregunta principal.
Evita mantener «does the bus leave» dentro de esta pregunta indirecta.
Could you tell me when the bus leaves?
Completa para expresar prohibición usando must
You ___ touch that wire. It is dangerous
You mustn't touch that wire. It is dangerous.
Mustn't significa «no debes»: tocarlo está prohibido. No significa que tocarlo sea opcional.
No confundas mustn't con don't have to.
You mustn't touch that wire. It is dangerous.
Completa con allowed para permiso futuro
From next month, you will ___ work from home
From next month, you will be allowed to work from home.
Will be allowed to expresa autorización futura. Significa: «A partir del próximo mes tendrás permiso para trabajar desde casa».
Be able to suele expresar capacidad o posibilidad; allowed hace explícito el permiso.
From next month, you will be allowed to work from home.
Wait for + persona o cosa significa esperar a alguien o algo. «Por favor, espérame».
From our old window, we ___ see the sea
From our old window, we could see the sea.
Could es natural con percepción, como see y hear, en descripciones pasadas. Significa: «Desde nuestra antigua ventana podíamos ver el mar».
La preferencia por managed to para logros concretos no elimina este uso de could.
From our old window, we could see the sea.
Completa con can't para expresar una regla
You ___ eat in the laboratory. It is forbidden
You can't eat in the laboratory. It is forbidden.
Can't puede indicar prohibición: «No se permite comer en el laboratorio». No solo expresa incapacidad.
No interpretes esta frase como una dificultad física para comer.
You can't eat in the laboratory. It is forbidden.
She ___ to start work at eight
She has to start work at eight.
En presente afirmativo, have to cambia a has to con he/she/it. Significa: «Ella tiene que empezar a trabajar a las ocho».
Have to se conjuga; can y must no añaden -s.
She has to start work at eight.
Give up significa rendirse o abandonar. «No te rindas. Inténtalo de nuevo».
Give in suele significar ceder; no es la expresión pedida aquí.
All visitors ___ wear safety glasses in this laboratory
All visitors must wear safety glasses in this laboratory.
Must expresa una obligación: todos los visitantes deben usar gafas de seguridad. Se construye con verbo base.
All visitors must wear safety glasses in this laboratory.
When I was seven, I ___ read music
When I was seven, I could read music.
Could expresa una habilidad general en el pasado: sabía leer música a esa edad. No describe un único intento.
No confundas habilidad habitual con un logro concreto.
When I was seven, I could read music.
500-page funciona como adjetivo delante de manual. Page permanece en singular.
Some people read novels to ___ from everyday worries
Some people read novels to escape from everyday worries.
Escape from significa escapar de algo; aquí se usa figuradamente para desconectar de preocupaciones.
Some people read novels to escape from everyday worries.
Forma el adjetivo con well + know
Well-known significa conocido. Usa el participio known, no knowing, y un guion en este adjetivo antes del sustantivo.
We spent the holiday on the ___, near the sea
We spent the holiday on the coast, near the sea.
Coast es la costa: la zona de tierra que bordea el mar. La expresión habitual es on the coast.
Evita «in the coast» en esta expresión.
We spent the holiday on the coast, near the sea.
I'll answer it. / I will answer it.
Will es natural para una decisión tomada al hablar: «Yo contesto». No era un plan anunciado antes.
Después de will usa answer, sin to.
I'll answer it. / I will answer it.
Completa con el verbo que significa resistir
Resist temptation significa resistir la tentación. Resist lleva el objeto directamente.
No añadas to entre resist y temptation.
Give up + verbo en -ing significa dejar de hacer algo. Aquí: «Nunca dejes de intentarlo».
They aren't going to move. / They are not going to move.
Con going to, niega be: are not going to. Significa: «No van a mudarse».
No uses «They don't going to move».
They aren't going to move. / They are not going to move.
Will probably y be likely to expresan una probabilidad parecida. Con they usamos are likely to.
Completa con el pasado de be allowed to. Expresa permiso.
At my old school, we ___ use calculators
At my old school, we were allowed to use calculators.
Were allowed to expresa que teníamos permiso en el pasado. Con we corresponde were.
No escribas «we allowed to» sin were.
At my old school, we were allowed to use calculators.
She doesn't able to come today
She isn't able to come today.
Be able to se niega con el propio verbo be: isn't able to. Significa: «Ella no puede venir hoy».
No uses doesn't en lugar de isn't con esta estructura.
She isn't able to come today.
I have never ___ able to ski
I have never been able to ski.
En presente perfecto usamos have/has + been able to. Significa: «Nunca he podido esquiar».
Can no tiene un participio que puedas colocar después de have.
I have never been able to ski.
Forma el adjetivo con left + hand
Left-handed significa zurdo. Describe a una persona que usa preferentemente la mano izquierda.
¿Qué diferencia hay entre «You mustn't buy it» y «You don't have to buy it»?
Mustn't buy it: no debes comprarlo. Don't have to buy it: no tienes obligación de comprarlo.
La primera prohíbe; la segunda deja la compra como opción. Cambiar una por otra cambia la instrucción.
La negación de una obligación no siempre significa prohibición.
I think people ___ live longer in the future
I think people will live longer in the future.
Will es habitual en predicciones basadas en opinión o creencia. Significa: «Creo que la gente vivirá más en el futuro».
I think es una pista contextual, no una regla que prohíba going to.
I think people will live longer in the future.
She ___ solve this equation without help
She can solve this equation without help.
Can expresa capacidad presente. Estructura: sujeto + can + verbo base. Significa: «Ella puede resolver esta ecuación sin ayuda».
She can solve this equation without help.
It's important to ___ the right choice
It's important to make the right choice.
Make a choice significa elegir o tomar una decisión entre opciones. Con the right choice: tomar la decisión adecuada.
It's important to make the right choice.
Completa usando need to. Expresa falta de necesidad.
She ___ to bring lunch; the company provides it
She doesn't need to bring lunch; the company provides it.
Con need como verbo ordinario, la negativa es doesn't need to + verbo base. Significa: «No necesita traer almuerzo».
She doesn't need to bring lunch; the company provides it.
Completa usando unlikely. Expresa que llegar antes de las seis es poco probable.
She is ___ to arrive before six
She is unlikely to arrive before six.
Be unlikely to significa «es poco probable que». No afirma que sea imposible.
Unlikely no equivale a definitely won't.
She is unlikely to arrive before six.
En esta negativa, probably suele ir antes de won't. Significa: «Probablemente no venga».
Succeed in + verbo en -ing significa lograr algo. In es una preposición; si la sigue un verbo, usamos -ing.
Evita «succeeded in pass» y «succeeded to pass».
Have patience significa tener paciencia. También puedes decir be patient, cambiando sustantivo por adjetivo.
Evita «be patience»: patience es un sustantivo.
Probably suele ir después de will y antes del verbo principal en afirmativas. Significa: «Probablemente lleguen tarde».
Evita colocar probably entre arrive y late en este ejercicio.
He may not come today. / She may not come today.
May not puede expresar que es posible que algo no ocurra. Aquí es una predicción incierta.
Según el contexto, may not también puede negar permiso; aquí se pide posibilidad.
He may not come today. / She may not come today.
Think about significa pensar en un tema o considerarlo. Aquí se consideran las opciones antes de decidir.
No traduzcas «pensar en» automáticamente como think in.
Succeed in significa tener éxito en algo. Después de in, finding mantiene la forma -ing.
Rise to the challenge significa estar a la altura del reto y responder a él.
Good leaders ___ responsibility for their mistakes
Good leaders take responsibility for their mistakes.
Take responsibility for significa asumir responsabilidad por algo.
Good leaders take responsibility for their mistakes.
I need to get rid ___ these old clothes
I need to get rid of these old clothes.
Get rid of significa deshacerse de algo. Aquí se refiere a ropa que ya no se quiere conservar.
I need to get rid of these old clothes.
Be good at + verbo en -ing expresa habilidad. Significa: «Es bueno resolviendo problemas».
Después de la preposición at no uses «to solve».
Elige la forma más natural para un logro concreto. Usa managed to o could.
The door was stuck, but yesterday I ___ open it after several attempts
The door was stuck, but yesterday I managed to open it after several attempts.
Managed to destaca que logré abrir la puerta en esa ocasión, pese a la dificultad. En afirmativas sobre logros concretos suele preferirse a could.
No generalices: could sí aparece en otros usos y con verbos de percepción.
The door was stuck, but yesterday I managed to open it after several attempts.
Completa con la forma de have to que indica que algo es opcional
Attendance is optional. You don't have to come.
Don't have to indica ausencia de obligación: no tienes que venir, pero puedes hacerlo.
No uses mustn't: eso prohibiría venir.
Attendance is optional. You don't have to come.
He can't drive. / He cannot drive.
Can se niega con can't o cannot. No necesita doesn't. Significa: «Él no sabe conducir» o «no puede conducir», según el contexto.
He can't drive. / He cannot drive.
Set goals significa fijar o establecer objetivos.
Evita «put goals» como traducción literal de poner metas.
Visitors are allowed to take photos.
Be allowed to + verbo base expresa permiso. Con visitors usamos are. Significa: «Los visitantes tienen permiso para tomar fotos».
Visitors are allowed to take photos.
She ___ able to speak French now
She is able to speak French now.
Be able to necesita be conjugado: I am; he/she/it is; you/we/they are. Significa: «Ella puede hablar francés ahora».
«She able to…» carece del verbo is.
She is able to speak French now.
May expresa posibilidad. Como modal, va seguido del verbo base, sin -s aunque el sujeto sea she.
La -s de tercera persona no se añade después de may.
Definitely suele ir antes de won't. El hablante afirma con seguridad que no volverá a ocurrir.
No confundas certeza negativa con una mera posibilidad negativa.
I tried several times, but I ___ open the file yesterday
I tried several times, but I couldn't open the file yesterday.
Couldn't puede expresar que no logré hacer algo en una ocasión concreta. La restricción habitual sobre logros afirmativos no se aplica igual a la negativa.
No supongas que couldn't solo sirve para hábitos pasados.
I tried several times, but I couldn't open the file yesterday.
I've already printed your ticket. You ___ print another copy
I've already printed your ticket. You needn't print another copy.
Needn't + verbo base indica que no es necesario hacer algo. Aquí equivale a don't need to print.
I've already printed your ticket. You needn't print another copy.
Completa con go usando going to
I ___ to the gym after class
I am going to go to the gym after class.
Am going to marca el plan; go es la acción de ir. La repetición es gramatical. También es natural «I'm going to the gym after class».
No elimines el segundo go si estás construyendo explícitamente be going to + go.
I am going to go to the gym after class.
Invierte can y el sujeto: can + sujeto + verbo base. Significa: «¿Sabes tocar el violín?».
No añadas do: «Do you can…?» es incorrecto.
She is going to study tonight.
La estructura es sujeto + am/is/are + going to + verbo base. Significa: «Ella va a estudiar esta noche».
Going to necesita el verbo be.
She is going to study tonight.
